item.statement_excerpt:
Assume Countable Choice. Use an actual balanced round-component complex model, with $m>0$ attaching circles $\gamma_j$, product torus $L$, at least two cut components, and standard integrable structure $J_0$ on $\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$. Suppose one proper cut component $A$ has exactly ONE boundary component, a single copy of $\gamma_i$. Its closure is the round disk complementary to the assigned round disk face in its sphere chart. Fix a node tuple $x=x_1+\cdots+x_m\in L$, $x_j\in\gamma_j$, and one marked source boundary point $p$.

The standard smooth holomorphic closed disks with node value $x$, actual component domain $A$ with coefficient one and zero elsewhere, have exactly ONE orbit under orientation-preserving conformal disk automorphisms fixing $p$. Their actual compact node-fixed linearization is surjective of real Fredholm index two, with kernel precisely the two infinitesimal node-fixing automorphisms. The same surjectivity and index hold in every actual weighted node-fixed realization of weight $0<\delta<\pi$ and every order when the protected exact node charts are used.

Take the actual smooth Hilbert family of protected structures based at $J_0$ in the proper-unit-domain regularity theorem, with $x$ among its prescribed node values. On a sufficiently small parameter ball, EVERY parameter has exactly one such disk orbit and it remains regular of index two in the same realizations. Thus its actual finite count modulo two is one. The radius may be chosen simultaneously for any finite list of such disk components and node tuples.

This computes the one-boundary-component base case only. It does not reduce a general component with several boundary circles to this case, compute its count, or supply target degeneration, attachment gluing, cancellation or Floer invariance.

proof_step_donor_fragments.exact_current_text: Every other attaching circle and every other node coordinate $x_j$, $j\ne i$, lies outside $\overline A$. Indeed $A$ is a component of the complement of the WHOLE attaching system with only the one boundary circle $\gamma_i$. A different circle inside it would be removed from that component and appear as further cut boundary; a different circle meeting its boundary would violate disjointness. Compactness gives positive separation. Choose a holomorphic coordinate $\chi$ on a neighborhood of $\overline A$ taking it to the closed unit disk and taking $x_i$ to one. It is explicit: for the exterior of a round face with center $a$ and radius $r$ use $r/(z-a)$ and a unit rotation; this includes infinity in its regular coordinate. Choose disjoint small complex coordinate disks about the other $x_j$, separated from that neighborhood. Their ordered product is a holomorphic symmetric-product chart along the whole image of the map $$u_0(z)=\chi^{-1}(z)+\sum_{j\ne i}x_j,$$ with source $p=1$. This is an actual smooth holomorphic disk of domain $A$ and node $x$, and its image misses the diagonal. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

Every other standard disk $u$ of that domain is of this form up to a node-fixing disk automorphism. Use the actual incidence cover in [F1]. On every nonconstant component its interior image lies in $A$: a point off the attaching circles outside $A$ would have positive degree where the total is zero, while an interior point on any attaching circle would, by openness, give nearby off-circle values on both sides. At a boundary point of $A$ one of those sides is outside $A$, since this component has the single separating boundary $\gamma_i$; all other attaching circles are outside $\overline A$. Thus the active interiors miss the whole circle system and lie in $A$. Their boundary values lie on $\gamma_i$. Over a physical boundary parameter, the tuple has exactly one entry on $\gamma_i$, by the definition of $L$. The boundary covering of the active components therefore has total degree one. Every component of $C$ covers the source disk and its boundary with the same positive covering degree, as proved in [F1]; hence there is exactly one active component and its projection $p$ has degree one. It is a disk biholomorphism, and the root $f$ on it maps onto $A$: every point of $A$ has degree one and therefore a preimage. Its active interior injectivity and nonzero derivative from [F1] make it a biholomorphism too. All other roots are constant and their node values force them to be the remaining $x_j$. Thus $u(z)=\chi^{-1}(\psi(z))+\sum_{j\ne i}x_j$ for a biholomorphism $\psi:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$ with $\psi(1)=1$. Such a biholomorphism is fractional linear: compose with the explicit Blaschke factor taking $\psi(0)$ to zero, then apply [F4] to it and its inverse; Schwarz equality makes that composition a rotation. It extends smoothly to the circle, and the condition at one is the actual node condition. Under a Cayley coordinate taking one to infinity, these automorphisms are precisely the positive affine maps. This proves the single-orbit classification against all actual integrable disks of the domain. [F1, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

Compute the actual operator at $u_0$ in the whole-image chart of step1.1. Rotate each inactive tangent line to $\mathbb R$. The target structure is $i$ throughout that chart, so the actual linearized differential operator is componentwise $D_0=\partial_x+i\partial_y$, with no zeroth-order coefficient. On the active boundary its line is $i e^{it}\mathbb R$; division by the constant $i$ makes it the scalar winding-$k=2$ line in [F2]. Each of the $m-1$ inactive components has the constant winding-$k=0$ line. Therefore the full node-free operator is onto with real index $3+(m-1)=m+2$. Its kernel evaluates onto all node tangent directions: the active kernel vector $i z$ takes value $i$ at one, spanning the active tangent line there, and each inactive constant real kernel vector spans its node tangent line. By the actual node-evaluation criterion in [F2], imposing zero node value preserves surjectivity and subtracts $m$ from the index, giving index two. Its kernel has real dimension two and contains the two independent infinitesimal automorphisms from [F2]; hence those are the entire kernel. Actual higher compact and weighted comparisons in [F2] give the same conclusions in all claimed realizations, not merely for formal Fourier coefficients. Source automorphisms transfer them to every disk in step2.1. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

We give the actual phase construction needed for perturbation, without differentiating composition on a full rough Sobolev mapping space. Use a global upper-half-plane source coordinate with node infinity, and the whole-image target chart $\Phi$ of step1.1. Write $\xi_1,\xi_2$ for the chart-valued derivatives of $u_0$ under source translations and positive dilations. They are real-linearly independent on every nonempty source open set: their active factors are the nonzero derivative of the disk Cayley map times $1$ and $z$. Choose a nonnegative smooth function $\rho$ of compact support in the source interior, positive on a disk, and define two real phase functionals on maps near $u_0$ by $$\ell_j(v)=\int\rho(z)\langle\xi_j(z),\Phi(v(z))-\Phi(u_0(z))\rangle_{\mathbb R}\,dx\,dy.$$ Their derivative on the affine kernel is the positive definite Gram matrix of $\xi_1,\xi_2$ with weight $\rho$. For a positive affine $g$ near the identity, the expression $\ell_j(v\circ g)$ is smooth jointly in $g$ and the actual $H^3$ map variable: change variables $w=g(z)$ in the integral, so all $g$ derivatives fall on the smooth compactly supported weight $\rho(g^{-1}w)\xi_j(g^{-1}w)|\det Dg^{-1}|$. The map $v\mapsto\Phi(v)$ is smooth in these $H^3$ charts by [F2]; the resulting weighted $L^2$ pairing is bounded. Thus the finite implicit theorem, or its actual Hilbert parameter version in [F3], supplies a unique small affine phase adjustment of every nearby map. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

Augment the actual node-fixed Cauchy–Riemann section by $\ell=(\ell_1,\ell_2)$. At $(a,u)=(0,u_0)$ its map derivative is $(P,d\ell)$. It is a bounded isomorphism: $P$ is onto by step3.1, its kernel is the affine two-plane, and $d\ell$ is invertible on that kernel by step4.1. A bounded inverse is obtained by first solving $P$ with its actual kernel-complement right inverse and then correcting by that finite kernel. The parameter theorem in [F3] therefore gives, for all sufficiently small $a$, one unique nearby phase-zero solution $u(a)$, smooth in the actual $H^3$ topology. It has the same node and domain: its configuration charts preserve the node and boundary torus, and their local-addition homotopy preserves the integer component degrees. Its zeros are actual smooth disks by [F2]. Surjectivity of $P$ persists by the Neumann inverse and continuity of the actual derivatives, and its Fredholm index stays two by the finite kernel/range block argument in [F2]. Every nearby actual zero can be phase-adjusted by step4.1 and hence belongs to this same orbit by implicit uniqueness. This proves local existence, regularity and local single-orbit uniqueness for every small parameter, with no generic-parameter assumption. [F2, F3, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

There are no additional distant disk orbits for arbitrarily small parameters. Otherwise choose $a_n\to0$ and a unit-domain disk $v_n$ not in the orbit of $u(a_n)$. Countable Choice selects this sequence. By [F4] reparametrize each by an exact node-fixing affine map so that a subsequence converges globally smoothly to a standard disk of this domain and node. Step2.1 identifies that limiting orbit with $u_0$; compose all reparametrizations with one fixed automorphism to make the limit precisely $u_0$. For large $n$ the reparametrized maps lie in the neighborhood of step5.1 and their small phase adjustments therefore equal $u(a_n)$. This contradicts their chosen different orbit. Hence after shrinking the parameter ball the one orbit in step5.1 is the full actual orbit set. It is regular of index two, and its mod-two count is one. [F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, construct, contradiction]

The weighted conclusions for these perturbed disks follow from [F2] because their node charts are protected and their actual compact node-fixed operators are onto of index two. For a finite collection of components and node tuples intersect the finitely many parameter neighborhoods, retaining one common smaller ball. All counts are of actual orbits classified and isolated above, not of formal domains presumed to have representatives. The argument computes this disk-component base case and its genuine local persistence; it makes no reduction from a many-boundary component and supplies no target or boundary-attachment gluing assertion. [F2, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct] ∎
